Blockwise edgeR GLM Quasi-Likelihood F-Test

bp_glm_qlf.Rd

Fits negative-binomial GLMs and runs quasi-likelihood F-tests on BPCells-backed counts by processing dense row blocks while preserving edgeR's global empirical Bayes shrinkage step. Both edgeR's legacy QL path (legacy = TRUE) and modern QL path (legacy = FALSE) are supported.

Usage

bp_glm_qlf(
  y,
  design,
  dispersion,
  offset = NULL,
  lib.size = NULL,
  coef = ncol(design),
  contrast = NULL,
  prior.count = 0.125,
  abundance.trend = TRUE,
  ave.log.cpm = NULL,
  block.size = 1000,
  workers = 1,
  keep.fitted = FALSE,
  robust = FALSE,
  winsor.tail.p = c(0.05, 0.1),
  poisson.bound = TRUE,
  legacy = FALSE,
  weights = NULL,
  keep.unit.mat = FALSE,
  ...
)

Arguments

y

A genes-by-samples count matrix.

design

Design matrix.

dispersion

Scalar or gene-level negative-binomial dispersion vector.

offset

Optional sample-level log-offset vector. Row-constant matrices are accepted and canonicalized to vectors. Gene-specific offset matrices are not yet supported.

lib.size

Optional library sizes used by edgeR::glmFit() when offset is NULL.

coef, contrast

Test specification passed to edgeR::glmQLFTest().

prior.count

Prior count passed to edgeR::glmFit().

abundance.trend

Logical scalar passed to the QL empirical Bayes trend.

ave.log.cpm

Optional precomputed average log CPM vector.

block.size

Number of rows to process per block.

workers

Number of row blocks to process in parallel.

keep.fitted

If TRUE, keep fitted values in the returned object.

robust, winsor.tail.p

Robust empirical Bayes options. robust = TRUE is not yet supported.

poisson.bound

Passed to edgeR::glmQLFTest().

legacy

Logical scalar. If FALSE, use edgeR's modern QL adjustment with streamed computation of the global average QL dispersion.

weights

Observation weights. Currently unsupported.

keep.unit.mat

Unit-level QL diagnostic matrices are not yet supported.

...

Additional arguments passed to edgeR::glmFit().

Value

A list containing the combined QLF table, GLM coefficients, quasi-likelihood shrinkage fields, and test metadata.
